stemMarkdown: A man travels from A to B at 45 km/h and returns along the same road at 72 km/h. What is his average speed (in km/h) for the whole journey? (Round to 4 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: Average speed is total distance over total time, not the average of the two speeds. Taking the one-way distance as $d$: time $= \dfrac{d}{45} + \dfrac{d}{72}$, so average speed $= \dfrac{2d}{d/45 + d/72} = \dfrac{2 \times 45 \times 72}{45 + 72} = 55.3846$.
altSolutionMarkdown: For equal distances the answer is the harmonic mean. The plain average $\dfrac{45 + 72}{2} = 58.5$ is the classic wrong answer, and it is always too high.
